title: Two smooth structures on the line
promptMarkdown:
Let $\mathbb{R}_1$ denote $\mathbb{R}$ with the smooth structure generated by the chart $(\mathbb{R},\mathrm{id})$, and $\mathbb{R}_2$ denote $\mathbb{R}$ with the smooth structure generated by the single chart $(\mathbb{R},\varphi)$, $\varphi(x)=x^3$.

1. Show that $(\mathbb{R},\varphi)$ is a chart (a homeomorphism onto $\mathbb{R}$), so that $\mathbb{R}_2$ is a smooth manifold, and show that the two smooth structures are different (the charts $\mathrm{id}$ and $\varphi$ are not compatible).
2. Show that the identity map $\mathbb{R}_1\to\mathbb{R}_2$ is smooth but is not a diffeomorphism.
3. Find a diffeomorphism $F:\mathbb{R}_1\to\mathbb{R}_2$ and prove that it is one, writing out both chart expressions.
4. Generalise: for any homeomorphism $h:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, show that $\mathbb{R}$ with the smooth structure generated by $(\mathbb{R},h)$ is diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}_1$. Then explain in at most three sentences the difference between "two different smooth structures" and "two non-diffeomorphic manifolds", and state (without proof) what Milnor showed about $S^7$.
hintLadder: Compatibility of $\mathrm{id}$ and $\varphi$ requires both $\varphi\circ\mathrm{id}^{-1}$ and $\mathrm{id}\circ\varphi^{-1}$ to be smooth on $\mathbb{R}$. One of them is a cube root.
To test smoothness of a map $f:\mathbb{R}_1\to\mathbb{R}_2$, compute $\varphi\circ f\circ\mathrm{id}^{-1}$; for a map $g:\mathbb{R}_2\to\mathbb{R}_1$, compute $\mathrm{id}\circ g\circ\varphi^{-1}$.
Look for $F$ whose chart expression $\varphi\circ F$ is the identity of $\mathbb{R}$.
For part 4, the same idea works with $h$ in place of $\varphi$: which map has chart expression equal to the identity?

checkExamples.label: correct LaTeX argument
checkExamples.text: $\mathrm{id}\circ\varphi^{-1}(y)=y^{1/3}$ is not differentiable at $0$, so the charts are incompatible and the structures differ. The identity $\mathbb{R}_1\to\mathbb{R}_2$ has chart expression $x\mapsto x^3$, smooth, but its inverse has expression $y\mapsto y^{1/3}$, not smooth. Take $F(x)=x^{1/3}$: then $\varphi\circ F(x)=x$ and $F^{-1}\circ\varphi^{-1}(t)=t$, both smooth, so $F$ is a diffeomorphism and the two manifolds are diffeomorphic although the structures differ.

checkExamples.label: plain-text with cube root words
checkExamples.text: The inverse chart map is the cube root, which fails to be differentiable at the origin; F(x) = cube root of x is the diffeomorphism.

checkExamples.label: wrong conclusion
checkExamples.text: Since the identity is not a diffeomorphism, R_1 and R_2 are not diffeomorphic.

checkExamples.label: no cube root at all
checkExamples.text: The identity map is smooth in both directions because x^3 is smooth, so the structures agree.
